name: Cannabullen Falls
description:
Leaders: Luen and Adrian
Date: Sunday 29 March 2026
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Join us for a scenic and adventurous day in Tully Gorge National Park, combining a bushwalk with a technical descent of Cannabullen Falls. We will walk in via the track, make our way to the falls, then abseil down before walking back out.

The approach is mostly on track, but sections may be overgrown, and there will also be some off-track travel near the falls. Expect a mix of straightforward walking, uneven ground, some rougher sections, and technical canyon-style movement around the waterfall area.

This is not a beginner abseil. Participants must be comfortable on steep terrain and have prior abseiling/rappelling experience. You will need to be confident following technical instructions, wearing a harness and helmet for extended periods, and moving safely around cliffs, wet rock, and slippery surfaces.

The day involves a solid return walk of about 14 km, plus the added time and effort of the abseil. A reasonable level of fitness is required.

Please bring appropriate gear for a full day outdoors, including sturdy footwear with good grip, water, food, and any personal technical gear if advised by the leaders. Final meeting details, start time, and gear requirements will be provided to those who RSVP.

Important: This trip is weather-dependent. Water levels and conditions at the falls will determine whether the abseil goes ahead.

name: Lookout Canyon
description:
Leader: Luen & Adrian
Date: 28th March at 10/11 am
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

This is a short but serious canyoning adventure in Girringun National Park, near Wallaman Falls. Lookout Creek Canyon features beautiful aqua pools, granite slabs, small waterfalls, scrambling, swimming, and a steep, difficult access and exit. Although the canyon itself is relatively compact, it is a technical trip that requires confidence in rough terrain and previous canyoning experience.

This is not a beginner trip. You must have prior canyoning, abseiling/rappelling, bushwalking, and scrambling experience, and be comfortable with exposure, slippery rock, steep off-track terrain, and moving efficiently as part of a group in a canyon environment. The exit is particularly steep and demanding, as we are taking the alternate exit due to the high flow at the moment.

The plan is to start at around 10:30 am, after the Wallaman Escarpment Walk, which is taking place earlier that day. This trip is suited to experienced members who want to back up for a second adventure, or who are happy to join just for the canyon.

Please come prepared with appropriate canyoning gear, sturdy footwear with good grip (i.e., canyoning boots), food, water, headlamp, and everything needed for a full afternoon in a remote and challenging environment. Final details, gear requirements, and meeting arrangements will be provided to those who RSVP.

Important: Weather and water levels will determine whether the trip goes ahead. The leader's decision on the day is final.

name: Learn to Lead - Wallaman Escarpment
description:
When: Saturday 28 March 2026
Location: Wallaman Falls escarpment, Girringun National Park
Leaders: Luen
Grade: 3-4 off-track (beginner-friendly terrain)
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com
Expressions of interest required

This walk is being run specifically as a leaders training day, following Cherry’s suggestion to build confidence and capacity within the Club. The aim is simple - create more walk leaders. This is not an exploratory epic, but a structured off-track day focused on decision-making, navigation, pacing, risk assessment and group management. If you are interested in gain some skills and leading some walks for the Club, then this is the walk for you. 

We will head to the Wallaman Falls escarpment for a half-day wander through open forest towards Butterfly Falls Lookout and views across to Hearts Falls. The terrain is generally forgiving - open woodland, light scrub and minor undulations - making it suitable for beginners who want to develop off-track skills in a manageable setting.

Everyone attending will navigate using GPS and map, and we will deliberately pause at key decision points to discuss route choices, hazards, turnaround triggers and contingency planning. The goal is mentoring in real terrain - not classroom theory.

This event is limited to members genuinely interested in leading future club walks. Participants should have attended a Club walk previously and willing to lead at least three trips for the Club.

Early start from Townsville (5:00 am departure), cooler air, clear objectives and a shared focus on building skills rather than just covering ground.

name: Trails and Ales - Castle Hill
description:
Stroll and Sip - The Ladies' Track
When: Friday 27 March 2026 - 5:30 pm
Location: Castle Hill, Townsville
Leader: Luen
Grade: 3
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Join us for a relaxed Friday after-work wander up the historic Ladies’ Track on Castle Hill - with a small twist. Bring one drink in your pack and we will enjoy a quiet sip together at the top before strolling back down the road to the cars.

We were rained out last time and cut it short, so hopefully this time we have better weather.

We will meet at the Cutheringa Trailhead lower car park at 5:30 pm sharp and take the Ladies’ Track up. The climb is around 2 km and takes roughly 30 minutes, following restored stone stairs, timber steps, and a contoured path cut into the hillside beneath the lower cliffs. This track traces a historic WWII-era route once used to access the Pill Boxes.

The pace will be easy and social, with time to pause, take in the views and enjoy a golden-hour moment at the summit. After our drink break, we will descend via the road for a straightforward return.

Bring:
- One drink of your choice (can, bottle or flask)
- Water
- Comfortable walking shoes
- A head torch, if you have one, just in case

A short climb, good company, and sunset over Townsville - not a bad way to end the week.

name: Mt Stuart Road fitness ride
description:
Mt Stuart Road fitness ride
📅Wednesday 18 March 2026 4:45 am
📍 Location: Mount Stuart

About this event
Mt Stuart Road fitness ride - Wednesday morning
Date: Wednesday 18 March 2026
When: 4:45 am
Location: Mt Stuart Road, Townsville
Leaders: Luen & Jodie
Grade: Intermediate fitness
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

The meeting location will be sent to those who RSVP.

Instead of our usual Tuesday Mt Stuart fitness walk, this midweek session will swap walking shoes for bikes. We will meet before dawn and ride the bitumen road all the way to the 584 m summit of Mt Stuart and back. It is a steady uphill grind followed by a fast, flowing descent, making it a great session for building climbing strength, fitness, and confidence on the bike. And a test for those insteaded in the bikepacking trip ahead.

This is a fitness ride and will start together but go at our own pace. Turn around after ~1 hour - TBD. Riders should be comfortable climbing on sealed roads and descending with control (ensure brakes are in working order and bike is serviced). Please bring a well-maintained bike, helmet, water, lights, and anything you need to manage a puncture or minor mechanical issue. As always, high-vis clothing is also recommended for low-light conditions.

name: Top of Jourama Falls - swim and picnic walk
description:
RSVP accepted via this platform - ❌
RSVP via email to walk leader directly - ✅👍
Please Note: Selecting Going on Facebook Events does not automatically register you for this event. Please contact the leader directly at info@veteducation.com.au (Cherry Judge) to secure your spot on this TBWC hike. This is important due diligence for our club insurance.

Top of Jourama Falls - swim and picnic walk
When: Sunday 15 March - 7:00 am
Location: Jourama Falls, Paluma Range National Park
Leader: Cherry
Grade: 3-4 (open to all levels - steep climb section)
RSVP: info@veteducation.com.au

Cherry will be leading a relaxed but adventurous day out to the top of Jourama Falls, with a swim and picnic as the main focus. The plan is to walk in via the lookout track, tackle the steady ~10-minute climb from the lookout, and then another ~50 min to the top of the falls. It is a steep and often hot ascent, so a reasonable level of fitness and comfort on hills is important.

At the top, we will enjoy time around the pools and cascades - perfect for a swim, a long lunch and soaking in the granite scenery. If conditions are safe and time allows, Cherry may explore a little further upstream along Waterview Creek, using the map as a guide and testing out some hands-on navigation.

This walk is open to all levels, but be prepared for heat, a sustained climb and uneven ground. Take your time, carry plenty of water and expect a social, exploratory day rather than a fast-paced mission.

Bring:
- At least 2-3 L of water
- Lunch and snacks
- Swimmers and towel
- Sturdy footwear with good grip
- Hat and sun protection

Meeting details will be provided once you RSVP directly to Cherry at info@veteducation.com.au.

A classic North Queensland combination: climb, cool off, eat well, repeat.

name: Dick Creek Falls (Stoney Creek tributary)
description:
Dick Falls, Mt Stuart
When: Saturday 7th - 7:00 am
Location: Mt Stuart - Roseneath area
Leaders: Wilfred & Luen
Grade: 4 (beginners with good fitness welcome)
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

We are heading to Dick Creek, a Stoney Creek tributary tucked into the Mt Stuart foothills near Roseneath. This one is a classic wet-season wander - an intermittent stream that comes alive after rain, with cascades, rock slabs and clear pools that only show their best side when North Queensland turns the taps on.

This is a Grade 4 walk suitable for beginners who are reasonably fit and comfortable on uneven ground. Expect rock hopping, creek crossings, some light scrambling and sections of off-track navigation. Distance and duration will depend slightly on conditions, but allow around 4 hours, including breaks and exploring.

The creek is intermittent, so flow will depend on rainfall. It should be running well with the recent rain we've had. We will explore upstream to a series of small waterfalls and pools. If it is lower, it is still a beautiful granite-lined creek system framed by open woodland and Mt Stuart’s rocky slopes.

Meeting details will be sent to those who RSVP.

Bring:
- At least 2 L of water
- Morning tea and lunch
- Sturdy footwear with good grip (expect wet rock)
- Hat and sun protection
- Swimmers and small towel if you would like a dip
- Dry bag for valuables (optional)

This is a relaxed but adventurous morning in one of Townsville’s underrated creek systems. A good introduction to off-track walking without committing to a full expedition.

To secure your spot, RSVP by emailing luenwarneke@gmail.com

Wet season creeks are short-lived performers. When they flow, they remind us how quickly this landscape shifts between dust and drama.

name: Remembrance Falls
description:
-------------------------------
**THIS WALK IS NOW FULL**
-------------------------------

Alright, Bushwalkers. 
This one is a proper wet-season gem.

Townsville Bushwalking Club Walk
Remembrance Falls - Paluma State Forest
Sunday 1 March 6:45am
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Wilfred and Luen will be leading a walk to Remembrance Falls in the southern section of Paluma State Forest. This is one of the largest waterfalls in that area - a striking, multi-tiered drop of around 50 to 60 m - and it is only worth visiting after decent rain. Early March should give us the best chance of seeing it in full flow.

This is a Grade 5 off-track walk. Expect approximately 10 km return and around 5 hours on foot, not including breaks. The route includes an overgrown logging road, steep descents into a mini gorge, a vegetated ramp, and some scrambling around the tiers of the falls (if not damp/raining). There is exposure in places and loose ground underfoot. Good fitness, confidence on steep terrain and solid bushwalking experience are essential.

We have sought and received permission for access through private property. We will meet near the base of the Paluma Range at 6:45 am. Exact meeting details will be sent once you RSVP.

The walk starts at 8am along Ewan Paluma Rd for those coming from Hidden Valley or who are making their own way to Paluma. Exact meeting details will be sent once you RSVP.

Wilfred will meet us there in his Troopie, which can carry up to 10 people. For those travelling in the Troopie, we will not need to arrange individual permits as we will be accessing under the approved permission. Spaces are limited to 10 - NOTE THAT THIS TROOPIE IS NOW FULL.

After descending into the gorge, we will explore the base of the multi-tiered falls and, conditions permitting, climb around the tiers to the top pools and lagoon. From there, we will head up to the ridgeline and plateau for views back across the forest and towards smaller nearby waterfalls before returning via the logging road and Taravale Road.

Bring:
At least 2 L of water
Morning tea and lunch
Sturdy footwear with good grip
Long sleeves and pants (lantana and thick vegetation in sections)
Swimmers and a small towel if you plan to swim

This walk is best suited to experienced off-track bushwalkers comfortable with steep terrain and light scrambling. Avoid this trip if you are unsure on exposed ground or recovering from injury.

To secure your spot, RSVP by emailing luenwarneke@gmail.com
Wet season waterfalls are a reminder that North Queensland is built on water, gravity and time. When they run, they run properly.
